patterns.name: pre_tp1_trailing_stop_required
patterns.description: Position monitor MUST have a trailing stop that activates BEFORE TP1 is hit. The standard trailing stop gates on tp1_hit=True, but TP1 may never be reached. Without pre-TP1 protection, positions that peak at +30-40% can reverse all the way to the hard stop, surrendering all unrealized gain.
patterns.rule: Add PRE_TP1_TRAILING_STOP_PCT (wider, e.g. 25%) that activates when position is up > PRE_TP1_ACTIVATE_GAIN_PCT (e.g. 15%), independent of tp1_hit.
patterns.anti_pattern: Trailing stop gated exclusively on tp1_hit

patterns.name: confluence_gate_requires_hard_override
patterns.description: Confluence gates that require multiple stored data fields (volume, buy pressure, liquidity) to block a sell are dangerous. When fields are absent, the bearish count stays at 0, permanently blocking the exit. ALWAYS pair any confluence gate with a hard price-action override (e.g., if dropped >X% from peak, sell regardless of signals).
patterns.rule: CONFLUENCE_HARD_REVERSAL_PCT (default 25%) must be checked BEFORE the signal gate. If crossed, sell unconditionally. Never let a data-absence cause a permanent hold.
patterns.anti_pattern: Pure data-signal confluence gate with no price-action fallback

patterns.name: mode_skip_must_preserve_state_flags
patterns.description: When a special mode (God Mode, etc.) suppresses a sell action, it MUST still evaluate whether that action was supposed to set a state flag. Skipping tp1 sell without setting tp1_hit=True breaks all downstream logic that gates on that flag (trailing stop, TP2, etc.).
patterns.rule: When God Mode skips TP1 sell: pos['tp1_hit'] = True. The sell is skipped, but the state transition still happens.
patterns.anti_pattern: sell_action = None without preserving the state flag the sell would have set
patterns.evolution_marker: 2026-03-28 | CRITICAL | Added from God Mode trailing stop gap

patterns.name: function_must_return_on_all_paths
patterns.description: Functions annotated with a tuple return type (e.g. -> tuple[float, str]) that fall through the end without a return statement will return None silently. This causes TypeError at the call site when unpacked, which can look like a data/provider error rather than a missing return.
patterns.rule: After writing any function that returns a tuple: verify the return statement exists at ALL code paths. Pay special attention to functions that log and then fall through (logging is often the last visible action).
patterns.anti_pattern: Function ends with a logger.info() call with no return statement below it
patterns.detection: AST scan: find functions with tuple return annotations, verify return statement at every path exit
patterns.evolution_marker: 2026-03-28 | CRITICAL | Root cause of NoneType unpack crash loop

patterns.name: live_sell_failure_must_escalate
patterns.description: When a live sell fails, silently logging and continuing leaves the position open at a loss with no retry mechanism. After N consecutive failures, escalate to CRITICAL log + Slack + wider slippage flag. Silent sell failures are invisible in production and result in held losing positions.
patterns.rule: Track pos['sell_failure_count']. At >= 3: CRITICAL log + Slack alert + pos['force_max_slippage']=True
patterns.anti_pattern: except Exception as e: logger.error(...) and move on
patterns.evolution_marker: 2026-03-28 | HIGH | Added from sell failure audit

patterns.name: nonetype_unpack_traceback_points_to_caller
patterns.description: TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object always shows the caller line, not the function that returned None. When hunting this error: find the unpack call site, trace to the function definition, verify return statement exists on ALL code paths — especially after logging calls at the end of a function.
patterns.rule: To find missing return: grep for all tuple unpack sites (a, b = func()), find the function, check for return at the very end.
